# One Place to Hide a Tile

Version 1.20.0 makes the card layout the only place to show or hide a tile. It also lets a blank title remove the header without leaving a gap.

## One place to hide a tile

- **The layout decides what is shown.** _[#126]_ Until now there were two ways to hide a tile: the Show Compass, Show Radar, Show History Chart and Show Map switches, or the eye icon in Card Layout. A tile hidden with a switch stayed in the layout, struck through. The switches are gone. The eye icon hides a tile, and the Hidden row brings it back.
- **The editor follows the layout.** The Compass and Radar, History Chart and Map sections only show while one of their tiles is placed. Before, they stayed visible for tiles that were hidden.

## Also in this release

- **A blank title hides the header.** _[#120]_ With `title: " "`, the card drew an empty header, which left a band of space above the first tile. On a map-only card, the map sat about twice as far from the top edge as from the sides. A title that is only whitespace now hides the header completely, and the map has the same padding on all four sides.
- **MapLibre 6.15.** The map library is updated from 6.13 to 6.15.

## If you already use the show switches

Your config carries over on its own. When the card loads, any of `show_compass`, `show_radar`, `show_history_chart` or `show_map` set to `false` becomes that tile's absence from `card_layout`. The keys are dropped, so dashboards look the same as before. The next save in the visual editor writes the new form. A compass whose radar was switched off keeps the full width.

In a YAML dashboard the old keys keep working, but you can replace them whenever it suits you. To hide a tile, leave it out of `card_layout`:

```yaml
card_layout:
  - compass: { width: full }
  - map: { width: full }
```

Thanks to @532910 for both reports.
